_description: Trivia difficulty guide and design principles for future question creation

easy.pattern: Constantly reiterated through dialogue, combat scenes, or character descriptors. Spans the full story.
easy.examples: Character weapons (katana=108 files), race (dogkin=142), pet names (Quinnie=68), key items (Soul Reaper=89)

medium.pattern: Arc-specific knowledge or periodic callbacks. Readers who paid attention during that arc will know it.
medium.examples: Arc villains (Venthros=26), class names (Child of Reckoning=18), character traits (Aurora daddy complex=12-15)

hard.pattern: One-shot or very rare mentions. Must be a BIG memorable moment — shocking, funny, or emotionally charged. Frequency alone does not qualify a question as hard; if the moment is forgettable, it is too punishing.
hard.examples: Iconic quotes (fucking my sister=1 file but unforgettable), exact prices (53 gold=1 file), lore one-shots (Lysaria volcano=1 file)

design_principles: Reward loyal and attentive readers, never punish them. The novel is 2M+ words — readers are not robots.
Memorability > frequency. A one-shot shocking scene can be hard-tier; a forgettable detail mentioned 5 times should not be.
Wrong answers should test story knowledge, not just be random. Use facts from other characters/scenes as traps (e.g. Ayame's 1 gold price as a wrong answer for Seraphiel's price).
Even hard questions should reference big moments. Avoid obscure numbers, dates, or technical details that no engaged reader would retain.
The story uses 'drug department' not 'narcotics' for Black Fang's division — match in-story terminology in questions and answers.
Current distribution: 99 easy, 91 medium, 73 hard. Game draws 10 easy, 9 medium, 6 hard per round of 25.
